title: Contrablend
author: Cary Ravitz
notes: The Caller's Box 219, permission: full. The dance M6's per-role progression exists for: the larks progress one place and the robins three, so the shadow the second roll-away leaves you beside is your new partner. `progression` and the second roll-away's `rebind` are what say so — and **until M8b the file loader dropped `progression` on the floor**, so every measurement of this dance before now was of a dance progressing both roles one place. It is read now, and the robins really do travel three places: at six couples `c0/robin` ends the time through 60 px along the set and `c0/lark` 20, which is "M1, W3". **B2's `who` stays `N1`, and the reason is the rebind.** B1's second roll-away carries `rebind: { partner: "shadow" }`, so by B2 your partner *is* your shadow and "you, your partner, your shadow and their partner" is three names for two people — the ring comes out degenerate and `relationRings` skips it. Read with the lattice partner instead it is four dancers strung along one line 60 px apart, which is not a circle. The four that really stand in a rectangle, and the four that hold your shadow, are you, your partner, your **neighbour** and their partner: `relationRing.test.ts` asserts that every dancer's own shadow is in their ring and that the gaps are 20, 20, 32, 32, 38, 38. So `N1` is the relation that *cuts* the set into the dance's own fours and "[with shadow]" is the transcript describing whom you find yourself circling with, which is M7's own reading of Whoosh's `circulate ... [with N2]`. The plain hands-four is not an option: it circles the original minor set and nobody circles with their shadow. **The ends are settled** (DD30): a waiting couple's `wait-out` now starts from where the dance really left those two dancers rather than teleporting them on to the waiting places, so the four end dancers who stand through B2's last thirteen beats no longer jump 32 px (the robins) and 37.7359 px (the larks) at the cycle boundary. Closure is **0.0000 px at every checked length**, where it was 37.7359 at five and six couples. **Two couples at two couples** (M9c): a waiting couple now takes the end of its hold it is actually standing at, rather than the end its station names, so the two dancers no longer walk through each other on the way in - and **at two couples the dance is green**, `collision 9.000 px` where it was 6.008. **Still owed, one thing, measured: `collision 0.000 px` at 3, 4, 5 and 6 couples**, at **beat 80**, the end of the second time through's A1. The progression re-pairs the set, A1's balance and swing resolves as two instances over one hands-four, and `resolve.ts`'s `homesOf` hands both of them the **same** pool of four home places: `placePairFor` then picks, per instance, with no knowledge of the other, and two of the four places are taken twice while two are left empty (`c0/lark ~ c1/robin` on one point). A swing settles on "the nearest two places that suit", which is right, and nothing de-conflicts the choice across instances, which is not. That is one mechanism and it is the same one Are You 'Most Done? is waiting for at its odd and long lengths. **M9g: the same measurement, and it is not the ledger either.** At four couples, beat 64, the `progressed` report is per dancer: the two wait groups are **0.0000 px** and the `p1` minor set's two couples are each **20.0000 px** out, on each other's places along the set - `c0/lark` wants `(16, 20)` and stands on `(16, 40)`, `c3/lark` wants `(-16, 40)` and stands on `(-16, 20)`. The per-role progression (larks one place, robins three) re-pairs the set every time through and the last figure, B2's `shoulder-round` with N2, does not leave the two couples the way round the shift names them. The `collision 2.5062 px` at beat 66.75 is downstream of exactly that: the waiting couple `w3` is `c0/robin` + `c2/lark`, and `c0/robin`'s body is a whole couple place up its own line from its wait station, so the straight walk in to the hold at `(-7, 60)` cuts through the minor set below (M9f measured the route via the station and lost two green lengths; not rebuilt here). Not promoted, and the one measured thing is `progressed` - 0.0000 at two and three couples, 20.0000 at four and five, 51.2250 at six.
